protections: P1: SVG served as image/svg+xml by the kernel must not carry active content (script elements, event-handler attributes, javascript:/data:text/html/data:text/xml hrefs, foreignObject); the only guard at the pin is util.RemoveScriptsInSVG, which removes elements named exactly 'script' (kernel/util/misc.go:235-272, check at misc.go:250), applied in getDynamicIcon (kernel/api/icon.go:167-169) and serveSVG (kernel/server/serve.go:620-622), and skipped when Editor.AllowSVGScript is on (kernel/conf/editor.go:22)

P2: user-controlled text placed into the generated dynamic-icon SVG markup must be escaped or neutralised (type 8 'content' is interpolated raw at kernel/api/icon.go:582-584; the 'color' value is already restricted to a palette or hex at icon.go:49-90)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: behind CheckAuth and serves the user's own uploaded assets; a fix scoped to getDynamicIcon (escaping content) looks complete
admin-only (CheckAdminRole) routes serving the user's own history and repo-diff snapshots
custom emojis are only embedded through , where SVG scripts do not run, and the route is authenticated
data/public is deliberately published, unauthenticated, user-placed content (issue 8593); sanitising it changes a documented feature
the helper already strips <script>, and a solver adding attribute or href filtering keeps the element-name equality test
the written file is sanitised when served through /assets, so the producer looks harmless
the query parameter is the visible input, and the template expansion of stored block title, name and alias (via text/template, no escaping) looks like trusted data

masking: At the pin both A and B are open: no SanitizeSVG exists anywhere in kernel/ (only util.RemoveScriptsInSVG at kernel/util/misc.go:235). Fixing A with a denylist (javascript:, data:text/html) masks B (data:text/xml), which stays exploitable through the same getDynamicIcon content sink (kernel/api/icon.go:584).

conflicts.what: Rejecting or stripping any '<' or '.action{' in type 8 content (the blunt fix for T1/T2) breaks the template icon feature at kernel/api/icon.go:538-540 and plain text icons. Escaping before the rune-length font-size calculation (icon.go:545-565) changes the rendered size for text such as 'A&B'.

If T1 is fixed by validating the raw query 'content' before RenderDynamicIconContentTemplate runs (icon.go:538-540), stored title/name/alias markup expanded afterwards is not covered. Escaping at the final interpolation (icon.go:584) closes both, so T9 is independent only when the T1 fix is placed on the input side.
Routing /public through the SVG sanitiser would alter deliberately published SVGs (serve.go:365-366); legitimate published SVGs with links or animations would change.

fairness_risks: Editor.AllowSVGScript=true must keep returning SVG scripts unchanged (kernel/api/icon.go:167, kernel/server/serve.go:620, kernel/conf/editor.go:22); a fix that sanitises unconditionally breaks a documented user setting.
/api/icon/getDynamicIcon is deliberately unauthenticated (kernel/api/router.go:36) because emoji tags load it (app/src/emoji/index.ts:28-29, 246). Adding CheckAuth is not a fair expected fix.
Type 8 must keep rendering plain text, CJK text and '.action{...}' template output (kernel/api/icon.go:538-584).

Legitimate asset SVGs use <a href="https://...">, <style> and <image href="data:image/png;base64,...">; an over-broad href or data: ban refuses shapes legitimate SVGs need. Tests should refuse data:text/xml, data:text/html and javascript: but keep data:image/png and https.
/public/ (serve.go:366) and /widgets/ and /plugins/ (serve.go:345-351) intentionally serve user-supplied active content; widgets and plugins are executable by design and must not be treated as traps.

design.why: T2 is the advisory anchor: the unauthenticated getDynamicIcon content sink, including the data:text/xml shape the report names. T4 (history and repo-diff raw SVG, dismissible as admin-only) and T5 (emoji raw SVG, dismissible because emojis load via ) are deepseek-type: the protection is absent and each has its own reason to dismiss. Each needs its own fix site in serve.go. T7 (namespaced script element surviving the name-equality check in the shared helper) is a mimo-type how-mechanism that stays open even after a solver strengthens attribute and href filtering. T10 should run as a hidden must-keep test (template and plain-text icons, AllowSVGScript=true, legitimate data:image/png hrefs) to catch over-hardening. This beats designs using T6 (a public-content feature conflict), T9 (independent only if the T1 fix sits on the input side) or T3/T8 (closed by the same helper fix as T7's surroundings and easily found from the report).

unverified: Fix commits d68bd5a79391 (A) and d01d561875d4 (B) were not readable from the pinned tree. The claim that the pin predates both rests on SanitizeSVG being absent from kernel/ and on the latest changelog being app/changelogs/v3.5.9/v3.5.9.md. What A's fix wrote, and whether B lives in it, is taken from the advisory summary only.

T7: that golang.org/x/net/html keeps a prefixed tag such as 'svg:script' as Data='svg:script' (so misc.go:250 does not match it), that html.Render re-emits a usable namespace declaration, and that the browser then executes it as an SVG script when served as image/svg+xml. None of this was executed.
T5: whether a non-admin or remote actor can place SVG files under data/emojis (no upload route was traced).
T9: that an unauthenticated caller can supply a block id whose stored title, name or alias carries markup that survives sql.BuildBlockFromNode (kernel/model/template.go:268-281); no test was run.
T8: whether AllowSVGScript or a non-/assets path ever serves files written by processHTMLBlockSvgImg without going through serveSVG.
